title: Pair-length check with a space bound
statement: For all natural numbers $C$ and $e$, there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)^{e+1}$ steps and outputs a single bit. The bit is true exactly when the aligned pair parser returns components $(a,b)$ with $|b|\le C(|a|+1)^e$, and false if parsing fails. At every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the computation on $x$ uses at most $c\big((|x|+1)^e+|x|+1\big)$ work-tape cells.
